warning: Historical lessons are evidence. Current rules override retired pricing, EV, CLV and old market-structure rules.
historical_market_note: XBH was not previously tracked as a first-class market in these historical cards; do not fabricate historical XBH predictions.

lessons: Separate bad outcome from bad process.
Candidate generation and market-specific research matter more than forcing picks.
Walk research needs hitter discipline plus pitcher command and bullpen context.
Market-specific park factors are required; generic good-hitting-park labels are inadequate.
Repeated statistics should come from one source-of-truth table to prevent sheet drift.
superseded: Any requirement that exact sportsbook price/EV/CLV is necessary for current prediction confidence.

lessons: Generic same-team correlation should not be assumed from tiny samples.
RR1 implementation produced illegal cross-team pairs; validation must be structural and deterministic.
RR2 should lock the best TB anchor and shift the walker, not the anchor.
Walk research must include pitcher handedness-specific command and hitter discipline context.
Do not refit a probability model from one small slate.
superseded: Price-gate and SGP-EV conclusions are historical only and are not current core requirements.

lessons: Do not replace a zero correlation prior with a positive prior after only a few observed pairs.
Low-sample pitchers require explicit uncertainty, not false neutrality.
Both starters and both lineups must be researched.
Lineup rescrub near first pitch is operationally important because projected players may disappear.
Confidence layers can separate stronger research from forced coverage.
superseded: Any price-based sleeper or pair evaluation requirement.

lessons: Projected lineups are valid research inputs when labeled honestly.
Starter/opening-role uncertainty must remain visible.
Bullpen state must be marked STALE when usage cannot be verified.
External projection/capper data is a cross-check rather than authority.
A PASS game can still contain research coverage without pretending it is strong conviction.
superseded: Best Price and Book columns are historical schema, not current core fields.

lessons: Official TBD starters remain blocking items.
Projected lineups and second-feed disagreements must be explicit.
Do not target a pitcher because ERA is ugly when strikeout/contact shape does not support the market.
Game-level side selection does not mean every player market belongs to that side.
superseded: Any price requirement in blocking/price/pen notes.

lessons: Old betting algorithm stays disabled.
Primary TB research performed substantially better than sleeper TB and HR on this slate.
Do not force sleeper/lower-order selections because a row exists.
Use lineup position as opportunity cost.
A good pitcher can still be a viable TB matchup when contact opportunity is high enough.
Full-game hitter props must account for starter workload and bullpen exposure.

slates.source: recent research revisions summarized in project history
lessons: Lineup filtering comes before player ranking.
Preserve DTD/IL/status tags and distinguish stale source tags from current official state.
Research both teams; a game thesis does not forbid strong individual props from the other side.
One player should not dominate multiple markets without independent market-specific mechanisms.
Projection-vs-rolling conflicts should be recorded rather than hand-waved away.
Sleeper labels do not create confidence by themselves.

cross_slate_current_lessons: TB emphasizes contact opportunity, expected PA, pitcher contact/K profile, bullpen path, then power as a second route.
Walks emphasize hitter patience plus pitcher command/count creation and bullpen/umpire context.
HR should be selective and mechanism-specific; do not force a homer pick in every game.
XBH is now a new independent market and must be modeled from doubles/triples/HR mechanisms rather than copied from TB or HR.
Rank continuous evidence; do not turn arbitrary thresholds into false gates.
Do not fade hitters because of recent unders.
Broad metrics should contextualize, not erase handedness, pitch mix, contact-inducing profile and market-specific signals.
